# SK2151 — A string equality test asks for invariant culture where ordinal was meant

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

An equality-shaped string operation is given StringComparison.InvariantCulture, which still runs the full linguistic comparison it was reached for to avoid.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Correctness |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, review it |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |
| Supersedes | CA1309 |

## Why

`StringComparison.InvariantCulture` is culture-*stable*, not culture-*free*. It still walks the collation tables, so it costs an order of magnitude more than `Ordinal` and it still answers `true` for sequences that are not the same string — a zero-width joiner and an empty string compare equal under it. For the things equality is actually asked about — identifiers, dictionary keys, protocol tokens, file names — `Ordinal` is what was meant. ⚠ **This is the mirror image of `SK2010`, and the harder one to see.** `SK2010` reports a policy that is *missing*; this reports one that is *stated and wrong*, which reads as deliberate and therefore survives review.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
if (string.Equals(scheme, "https", StringComparison.InvariantCulture)) { }
```

Write:

```csharp
if (string.Equals(scheme, "https", StringComparison.Ordinal)) { }
```

## When it does not fire

⚠ **`CultureInfo.InvariantCulture` is never reported, and the exclusion is structural rather than a filter.** Invariant culture is *correct* for round-tripping formatted data — `value.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)`, `decimal.Parse(text, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)` — and a rule that could not tell the two apart would be advising authors to corrupt their own serialisation. This rule keys on the `System.StringComparison` enum, which formatting and parsing APIs do not accept, so a `CultureInfo` argument cannot reach it. ⚠ **Ordering is excluded on purpose.** `Compare` and `CompareTo` are silent: a comparison whose result feeds a sort is the one place linguistic collation is legitimately wanted, and a sort that must not be linguistic is a design decision rather than a slip. Only the equality-shaped members are inspected — `Equals`, `StartsWith`, `EndsWith`, `Contains`, `IndexOf`, `LastIndexOf`. ⚠ **`fixIsSafe: false`**: swapping the enum member changes what the program computes, and where the author really did want stable linguistic semantics the honest replacement is `CurrentCulture`, which no analyzer can choose for them. ⚠ `CA1309` covers this ground and is **off by default** on a plain project — see the measurement in doc 08.
